mutant.description: A mutant root outside every worktree holding copies of the record and the check, with the BASELINE run there first and reading PASS on all three. Three mutants, one per criterion: (1) artifact_versions_count set to 3 while the list holds 2; (2) outcome left FOUND while rollback_artifact.content_sha256 was swapped to the OTHER version's digest, so the claimed rollback artifact no longer matches the live function; (3) a genuine write appended to commands, s3api copy-object.
mutant.expected: AC1 FAIL on (1), AC2 FAIL on (2), AC3 FAIL on (3)
mutant.observed: (1) FAIL: artifact_versions must list every version with its version_id and content_sha256, and state the count | AC1 FAIL rc=1. (2) FAIL: FOUND needs a version id whose content digest equals the live digest, re-read by head-object | AC2 FAIL rc=1. (3) FAIL: a recorded command matches the write pattern \\bcopy-object\\b | AC3 FAIL rc=1. Each was reverted and all three re-read PASS. Mutant (2) is the one that matters: it is the exact way this record could be wrong and still look complete -- a plausible digest in the rollback field that belongs to the wrong version.

determinism.method: The deciding digest was taken from CONTENT, not from metadata: each version was downloaded with get-object --version-id into a new empty folder outside the repository and hashed locally to base64 sha256, the CodeSha256 form. The object's own content-sha256 metadata and its ETag were then read separately with head-object and used only as corroboration. The artifact address was read from the source map rather than typed, and the version list was filtered and counted client-side.
determinism.observed: Three independent agreements on the found version: the locally computed digest of its bytes, the object metadata's content-sha256, and the source-map entry's artifact_sha256 and deployed_code_sha256 -- all four values equal YpE2MyUwdGzMfLaUGXi8cClxoVHFFmOz5LT1BYmoTa8=, which is also the live function's CodeSha256. The non-matching version's digest differs in both the computed and the metadata reading, consistently. Its LastModified also sits 3 m 24 s before the function's, the shape expected of the upload that made it live.

declared_exclusions.reason: Out of scope and explicitly not settled by this record. Row IRPT_ANLREQ-D2-W53-S3 is that 21 of the 28 live members have no blob in git; this cell gives a rollback TARGET, not a rebuild path. Stated in the record so the finding cannot be read as more than it is.

declared_exclusions.item: A row for the noncurrent-expiry reading
declared_exclusions.reason: The order says a lifecycle rule that would expire the found version is a row. There is none: the bucket's only rule aborts incomplete multipart uploads after 7 days and carries no NoncurrentVersionExpiration or Expiration action, so no row is owed. The MPU rule is recorded anyway so the reading is not mistaken for 'no lifecycle configuration at all'.
